problem:
A body of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons. At time $t\ge 0$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t)=\frac{1}{12}{t}^{4}+\frac{1}{6}{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}+6t+12$ meters.

Calculate the time ${t}_{∗}$ at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude. Do not round the answer.

${t}_{∗}=$

{{field-1}} $\text{s}$

feedback.problem:
A body of mass $1\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\ge 0$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t)=\frac{2}{3}{t}^{3}-8t$ meters per second.

Calculate the time ${t}_{∗}$ at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude. Do not round the answer.

${t}_{∗}=$

{{field-1}}  $\text{s}$
feedback.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F(t)=ma(t),
$$

 
where $F(t)$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a(t)$ is the acceleration. 

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{3}{t}^{3}-8t) \\  & =2{t}^{2}-8\end{aligned}
$$

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set $a(t)=0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}-8 & =0 \\ 2{t}^{2} & =8 \\ {t}^{2} & =4 \\ t & =\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\ge 0,$ we disregard the negative solution. 

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude at ${t}_{∗}=2\,\text{s}.$
